brief: A single hex base, nothing else added beside or on top of it, with five drawers in it.

requirements.requirement: Single hex base, nothing else added beside or on top of it
requirements.evidence: Build contains exactly one piece: piece:0,0,0;half-n at 0,0,0 level 0. No neighboring cells and no level 1 piece. check_build shows 3 open cap faces but no errors.

Configurator allows at most one drawer per half-base cell (find_sockets for drawer on half-n offers a single socket 's' at the cut face). Full hex bases offer zero drawer sockets. Notch/bay drawer frames require 2-3 adjacent bases (empty position beside two/three cells) which would violate 'nothing else beside'. Applied one drawer (drawer:0#0,0#cut) – the maximum the socket rules permit for a single isolated base. Five drawers in one cell is blocked by SOCKET_OCCUPIED / no-offer rules.

finish.summary: Built a single half-hex base (half-n) with the only drawer the configurator permits on an isolated cell (1 drawer). Five drawers in a single base is not possible under current placement rules: full bases take 0 drawers, half bases take 1, and notch/bay frames need additional bases beside the drawer, which contradicts the 'nothing else beside or on top' restriction. Build is mesh-clear.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
